newsitem.title: USA: Seagate stock tumbles after announcement.
newsitem.headline: Seagate stock tumbles after announcement.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc. stock tumbled Tuesday after the maker of computer disk drives warned that earnings for the latest quarter would not meet expectations on Wall Street.
Seagate stock fell $3 to $39.375 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Seagate, based in Scotts Valley, Calif., said Monday after the stock market closed that demand had weakened for its high-performance drives. The company is one of the nation's largest makers of disk drives, which store massive amounts of data in personal computers, workstations and servers, the computers that anchor computer networks.

In a brief statement issued late Monday, Seagate said revenues for the quarter ended in June are expected to be 6 percent to 10 percent below the $2.5 billion reported for its third quarter ended in March.

The company also said earnings before one-time charges could fall short of the third quarter's profit of $1.01 a share. Wall Street analysts had expected the company to earn $1.06 a share in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to the First Call service.
In the year-ago quarter, Seagate earned $101 million, or 92 cents a share, on revenues of $2 billion.

Seagate Chairman Al Shugard said Monday the weak demand was restricted to the high end of the market for drives for servers, where Seagate has been losing sales to competitors, and not in the personal computer market.
